_notes.price: NT$49.05 close 2026-10-30 (Yahoo TW; MoneyDJ engine page via Fubon e-broker: market cap NT$869,338m)
_notes.shares: 16,192m pre-merger (share capital NT$161.92bn at NT$10 par) + 1,531.5m issued 2026-09-01 to Mercuries Life holders (5,899.5m x 0.2596) = 17,723.5m; matches market cap / price
_notes.book_value: ESTIMATE, Sep-30-2026 post-merger: Jun-30 equity NT$281,740m (reported BVPS 17.40, MoneyDJ; assumed net of the NT$22.7bn 2025 dividend, ex-date 2026-07-01) + 3Q26 net income NT$10,420m (9M 31,850 - 1H 21,430, company monthly releases) + fair value of shares issued NT$60,758m (1,531.5m x NT$39.67, the Aug-2026 P/B 2.28 x 17.40 per HiStock). 3Q26 OCI is NOT included; a bargain-purchase gain or goodwill is not known until the 3Q26 statements. BVPS ~NT$19.91. The valuation is anchored on earnings (Y1 net income = ROE 13.5% x this book = NT$47.6bn): a purchase-price allocation that changes book but not earnings or distributable capital does not change value, so book is re-based, not re-valued, when 3Q26 is out.
_notes.cost_of_equity: 6.06% = TWD riskless 1.51% (Taiwan 10Y 1.99% on 2026-10-30 less Taiwan default spread 0.477%, Damodaran Jul-2026) + beta 1.0 x ERP 4.55% (Damodaran implied US ERP 4.20% on 2026-10-01 vs a 5.29% T-bond, held at the 10-30 yield of 4.94%). BETA IS A JUDGMENT, NOT A MEASUREMENT. Sourced industry (levered) betas, Damodaran Jan-2026: money-center banks Global 0.70 (604 firms; 2021-26 average 0.42), EM 0.59 (455; avg 0.41), US 0.76 (15); life insurers Global 0.80, EM 0.82, US 0.64. Weighted by E.SUN's post-merger equity (bank ~83%, life ~17%) the bottom-up beta is 0.72 (EM basis 0.63). We do not use it: at beta 0.72 the cost of equity (4.79%) is only 2.3pp above long-run growth, the terminal value carries 81% of the value above book (engine warning), and Base is worth 2.9x book with event risk (4.7x without), above the 2.82x maximum E.SUN has traded at in five years. Beta 1.0 gives 2.07x with event risk. The industry-beta result (TP NT$59.7, Buy) is reported as the main alternative. Local regression beta 0.12 (MoneyDJ, vs TAIEX) rejected: TSMC is ~42% of TAIEX. Taiwan event risk sits in the hazard overlay, not in the discount rate.
_notes.hazard: 1.5%/yr, 90% loss of equity (a bank's book is a claim on the same economy); applied to every dividend (DDM form)
_notes.roll_forward: 12-month TP = fair value x (1 + cost of equity) - NT$1.69 dividend (2026E EPS 2.595 = 9M 1.95 + 4Q26E NT$11.43bn / 17,723.5m shares; x 65% payout; paid ~Jul-2027)
_notes.roe_history: ROE 2021 10.96%, 1H22 7.52%, 2024 10.66%, 2025 13.04%, 1Q26 14.43%, 1H26 15.46% (company releases); 1H26 net fee income +39.9%, wealth-management fees +30.7%
_notes.dupont: ROE = ROA x leverage. Leverage 17.0x = 1H26 ROE 15.46% / ROA 0.91% (company); 2021 16.6x, 2024 15.7x, 2025 16.3x. ROA 2021 0.66%, 2024 0.68%, 2025 0.80%, 1H26 0.91%. Post-merger leverage not disclosed until the 3Q26 statements.
_notes.scenarios: Base ROE 13.5% (2027) -> 12.5% -> 12% steady: fee income normalises from a bull-market peak (1H26 net fees +39.9%) but stays above 2021-24 (~10.7%) with Mercuries Life and the wealth franchise. Bull holds 14-15% (fees structurally higher, bancassurance synergies). Bear: market correction in 2028 (ROE 8.5%; 1H22 was 7.52%), then 10.5% (2021-24 level). Payout 65% (2025: NT$1.4 / EPS 2.12 = 66%).
_notes.model_years: Year 1 = 4Q26-3Q27 (opening book at 2026-09-30, discounted from the 2026-11-01 valuation date), not calendar 2027.
